children: Pay settlements by British employers edged up in the three months to the end of September but there was little sign of a shift in wage trends, human resources data firm Brightmine said on Wednesday.
The median pay award by employers rose to 3.1%, up from 3.0% in the previous three-month periods to August and July but lower than the pace of increases seen earlier this year.
On Tuesday, official data showed private sector wage growth rose for the first time since the end of 2024, adding to the case for a Bank of England interest rate hike in November.
Below are details from the survey:
Most pay deals did not exceed those given a year earlier
Pay awards were expected to stay at 3% in 2027
Higher employer social security contributions are constraining employers
An increase in the minimum wage could also stretch budgets
Brightmine analysed 42 pay settlements between July 1 and September 30 covering more than 650,000 employees.
